channel.title: Latest alerts from washingtonpost.com
channel.description: An unofficial feed created by Derek Willis.

item.title: Trump's approval rating hits record low, handing Democrats a clear midterm edge, Post-ABC-Ipsos poll finds
item.description: The president’s approval among U.S. adults is at 33 percent, with 66 percent disapproving and just over half saying they disapprove strongly. In the competition for control of the House, Democrats hold an eight-point lead among registered and likely voters, an improvement since The Post’s July poll.

item.title: Two people killed, including 6-year-old boy, and multiple injured in Wichita as vehicle drives onto field during soccer game
item.description: Authorities who responded to the incident at the Stryker Sports Complex found community members rendering medical aid to the injured and a truck on the field, with the driver still inside, along with two juveniles. A 34-year-old woman is in custody and cooperating, they said, and at least 10 people with traumatic injuries were taken to hospitals.

item.title: A filmmaker spent years in an Elon Musk rabbit hole. Conclusion? ‘Sociopathic.’
item.description: As the tech titan’s power grew, “he became more and more self-centered,” said Alex Gibney, director of a mammoth new documentary that opened Friday.

item.description: President Donald Trump has made no secret of his demands to see charges against former officials.

item.title: A blood test for 50-plus cancers? One survivor is glad he took it.
item.description: The FDA is expected to approve a new kind of blood test that may allow earlier diagnosis and less invasive, more effective treatment. But doctors warn of drawbacks.

item.title: Rep. Ilhan Omar’s lawyers say authorities ignored judge’s restrictions on home search
item.description: In a letter obtained by The Washington Post, attorneys for the Minnesota Democrat condemned a Justice Department inquiry into her immigration history as a politically motivated attack.

item.title: Pope Leo leaves hospital after lung cancer operation
item.description: The pope waved to the crowds as he left the hospital to return to the Vatican, appearing in public for the first time since his admission.

item.title: Teacher and alert father helped save lives in Oregon school shooting, police say
item.description: A female teacher tackled the 16-year-old gunman who shot his way through security doors with a pump-action shotgun at Silver Rail Elementary School. The father of two students at the school, who minutes earlier had seen the teenager shoot into a nearby vehicle, then approached the pair with his own gun and killed the shooter. Bend Police Chief Michael Krantz said their quick thinking saved lives and was exemplary of “true heroism.”

item.title: Amtrak is making some big changes. Here’s what passengers can expect.
item.description: Sleek new Airo trains are coming to the East, route options are being expanded again, and a new lounge is being built at Washington’s Union Station.

item.title: Painting the Eisenhower building would harm the White House-adjacent landmark, Trump administration acknowledges. It still wants to.
item.description: Covering the building’s granite with white paint would fundamentally alter its original appearance, diminish its architectural value and adversely affect the historical area where it’s located, according to a draft environmental assessment released Friday.

item.title: Oregon school shooter fired into special education class Thursday, according to relatives of children at the elementary school
item.description: The assailant was fatally shot at the scene, killed by a man who has two children in the school and had a concealed weapon, neighbors and parents said.

item.title: Palestinians and Washington Post photographer attacked in West Bank
item.description:
Militant settlers attacked Palestinians trying to harvest olives and severely beat Heidi Levine, a veteran photographer.
Matt Murray, executive editor of The Post, said in a statement, "While we are relieved that Heidi has received medical care and is safe, we are outraged by this unwarranted attack on a journalist doing her job and urge a thorough investigation and follow-through from authorities.”

item.title: Judge extends White House access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico while lawsuit over media ban proceeds
item.description: U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly issued a preliminary injunction late Tuesday, supplanting a temporary restraining order he granted Sept. 24. The move allows the outlets to maintain regular access to White House grounds while litigation continues. President Donald Trump last month barred the organizations from the White House for reporting what he called “fake news.”

item.title: Investigation of Rep. Ilhan Omar focuses on her birth date and decades-old immigration paperwork, people familiar said
item.description: The Minnesota Democrat, who was born in Somalia and fled civil war there with her family before immigrating to the United States in 1995, has repeatedly rejected allegations that her documents used to secure legal status and U.S. citizenship contained falsehoods. Such claims have circulated in conservative media for years, and she dismissed them again this week as “baseless lies and smear campaigns.”

item.title: OpenAI employee arrested by FBI after “sophisticated” recording device was found in an executive conference room
item.description: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old citizen of Saudi Arabia who has been working at OpenAI since July 2025, was arrested Oct. 9 and appeared in federal court Tuesday. OpenAI is one of a handful of companies at the cutting edge of developing highly capable artificial intelligence models.
